verdicts.reasoning: wattāḇōʾ ḇî rûaḥ: anarthrous noun with a feminine verb, agent of wattaʿămiḏēnî. Diverges from ASV 'the Spirit'; transliteration under the inferred overlay rule leaves the wind/spirit/divine-spirit question open rather than importing the capital, and the Hithpael participle middabbēr is correctly 'the one speaking'.

MT ʾel-gôyim hammôrəḏîm kept against the LXX (no 'nations') and the commentators who delete it as a gloss; the MT construes and the variant is recorded. bənê yiśrāʾēl 'sons of Israel' and ʿad-ʿeṣem hayyôm 'to this very day' are exact; the speech opens here and closes at 2:8.
qəšê p̄ānîm wəḥizqê-lēḇ rendered literally ('hard of face and strong of heart') where the ASV paraphrases; the ḥzq wordplay is real. The messenger formula is correctly nested in single quotes.
ʾim-yišməʿû wəʾim-yeḥdālû 'whether they hear or whether they refrain' (ḥāḏal 'cease, hold back') and bêṯ məri 'a rebellious house' are exact; nāḇîʾ 'prophet' applies the central entry.
sārāḇîm wəsallônîm 'briers and thorns' keeps the ASV; the note honestly records the uncertain Aramaic derivation ('rebels'). ʾal-tēḥāṯ 'do not be dismayed' (Niphal of ḥtt) is correct.
kî məri hēmmâ 'for they are rebellious' renders the MT abstract noun; the witnesses with 'a rebellious house' are recorded and the MT kept under the baseline.
šəmaʿ ... ʾal-təhî-meri kəḇêṯ hammeri, pəṣēh p̄îḵā weʾĕḵōl: 'hear ... do not be rebellious like the rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat' is exact; the speech of 2:3-8 closes correctly.
wəhinnēh-yāḏ šəlûḥâ (Qal passive participle) 'a hand was stretched out'; məḡillat-sēp̄er 'a scroll of a book' modernizes ASV 'roll' with no change of sense (overlay megillat entry, direct).

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked every English line, with particular attention to the 16 reception-note sites (2:1, 2:10, 3:3, 3:12, 8:3, 11:1, 11:23, 40:2, 40:3, 42:14, 43:2, 44:2, 44:3, 44:15, 44:18, 44:30). No line carries the canon reading: kāḇôḏ stays 'glory' (11:23; 43:2), the bronze man keeps the Hebrew simile (40:3), qōḏeš stays 'holy' against the canon's 'healthful' (42:14), ʾûlām stays 'porch' against the 'airlock' reading (44:3), and yezaʿ is rendered by its accepted sense (44:18). Each reception note was checked against the TBWTT ch. 3 quotation file and is accurate and labelled, except that 11:23 slightly overstates the canon (verdict revise, notes only). Two features a cold reader might query were judged not to be leakage: 'ruach' (an inferred overlay convention that leaves an acknowledged ambiguity open and replaces the ASV's doctrinal capital) and 'between the land and the skies' at 8:3 (the ratified eretz default and shamayim physical register, identical to GEN-WOH 1:1, with the Hebrew's 'in visions of Elohim' kept). The sacrificial and architectural modernizations ('guilt-offering', 'dash', 'guardroom', 'vestibule', 'altar hearth') follow NRSV/NJPS and the lexica and carry no interpretive content.

Spot-checks the report requested: NRSV 8:16 'temple', 42:1 'temple yard', 42:3 'in three stories', 43:15-16 'altar hearth', Yadin IEJ 8 (1958), the Mesha line-12 ʾrʾl, and Albright 1942 (ziggurat; arallû) are consistent with the reviewer's knowledge; the '43:3 six manuscripts' count and the exact LXX figure at 40:14 could not be confirmed independently and should be checked against BHS or worded as 'some manuscripts' / 'a different figure' (non-blocking). founderDecisionRecommendations.A-quotation-marks: Ratify the Kings convention for Ezekiel. The reviewer's own stack simulation confirms all eight chapters balance and the 43:7-17 boundary is defensible. Schedule a punctuation-only pass on ch. 37 (37:4-5, 9, 12-14, 16, 19, 21-28) and a check of chs. 1 and 10 so the book ships with one convention.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-proper-names: Keep English forms in Ezekiel for this wave: a mixed book would be worse than either practice, and the three signed-off chapters already use English. Recommendation for the corpus decision: the Latter Prophets volumes (isaiah-woh, ezekiel-woh, daniel-woh) already share English forms while genesis/exodus/Kings transliterate; record that genre split explicitly in a central convention note rather than converting Ezekiel, unless the founder wants decision A extended corpus-wide, in which case the mechanical pass over all eleven chapters is straightforward.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-ruach: Ratify the overlay rule for agent/transport rûaḥ, 'spirit' for human idioms and 'side' for the compass sense, and support merging it with the Kings ruach entries into one central entry. Before promotion, narrow the 'gift' clause: rûaḥ ḥăḏāšâ paired with lēḇ (11:19; later 18:31; 36:26a) is the human disposition and should be 'a new spirit', while YHWH's own rûaḥ and the breath of life (36:27; 37:5-6, 14) stay 'ruach'. Verse flag at EZK-WOH-11:19.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-inferred-temple-terms: Ship both as inferred. ʾêlām 'vestibule' (NRSV) and harʾēl/ʾăriʾêl 'altar hearth' (NRSV) are lexically supported, replace ASV renderings without lexical basis ('arches', 'upper altar'), and the disputes (40:30 plurals; the 'mountain of El' vocalization) are recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-sacrificial-vocabulary: Ratify the new central entry as direct. 'guilt-offering' and 'dash' are lexically motivated and match NRSV/NJPS and isaiah-woh; Milgrom's alternatives are correctly recorded but not adopted. Add the glossaryRef to EXO-WOH-20:21 and 1KI-WOH-8:63-64 at the next pass of those books.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-refId-prefix: Agree. Normalize EZK- to EZK-WOH- (and GEN- to GEN-WOH-) in one dedicated mechanical central op with a before/after count, separate from any content diff, and only after the Revelation and Ezekiel E2 diffs are both applied.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן־אָדָם֙ עֲמֹ֣ד עַל־רַגְלֶ֔יךָ וַאֲדַבֵּ֖ר אֹתָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you."

notes.official:
*ben-ʾāḏām* 'son of human' is the book's form of address to the prophet (some ninety times), kept as in the signed-off chapters (`ben-adam`; ASV 'son of man'). *ʿămōḏ ʿal-raḡlêḵā* 'stand on your feet' answers 1:28, where the prophet has fallen on his face.

The quotation marks are editorial; Ezekiel follows the Kings convention (double quotes for speech, single quotes for speech within speech, a speech kept open across verses until it ends) under the overlay entry `direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-ezekiel`.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes 2:1 and 2:8 ('Son of man, stand upon thy feet, and I will speak unto thee ... eat that I give thee'), takes the speaker to be one of the creators, and reads the eating of the scroll as intellectual nourishment. The line renders the Hebrew lexically.

paragraphs.text: וַתָּ֧בֹא בִ֣י ר֗וּחַ כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר אֵלַ֔י וַתַּעֲמִדֵ֖נִי עַל־רַגְלָ֑י וָאֶשְׁמַ֕ע אֵ֖ת מִדַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלָֽי׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And ruach came into me as he spoke to me, and it set me on my feet; and I heard the one speaking to me.

notes.official:
*wattāḇōʾ ḇî rûaḥ* 'and ruach came into me'. *rûaḥ* has no article and takes a feminine verb; it is the agent that sets the prophet on his feet, as again at 3:24. ASV has 'the Spirit entered into me', NJPS 'a spirit entered into me', and NRSV 'a spirit entered into me'. The Hebrew does not say whether the force is a wind, a breath or the divine spirit, and the ASV capital brings in the later doctrine of a personal Holy Spirit. The book's practice, set at 37:1 ('by the ruach of YHWH') and now recorded in the overlay entry `ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`, is to transliterate where rûaḥ enters, lifts or carries the prophet. Block ('The Prophet of the Spirit: The Use of rwḥ in the Book of Ezekiel', *JETS* 32, 1989) lists this verse among the uses of rûaḥ as the agent that animates the prophet.

*middabbēr* 'the one speaking' is a Hithpael participle (assimilated *mitdabbēr*). The same form is used of the divine voice at 43:6 and Num 7:89.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י בֶּן־אָדָם֙ שׁוֹלֵ֨חַ אֲנִ֤י אֽוֹתְךָ֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־גּוֹיִ֥ם הַמּוֹרְדִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָרְדוּ־בִ֑י הֵ֤מָּה וַאֲבוֹתָם֙ פָּ֣שְׁעוּ בִ֔י עַד־עֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, I am sending you to the sons of Israel, to nations that are rebelling, who have rebelled against me; they and their fathers have transgressed against me to this very day.

notes.official:
*ʾel-bənê yiśrāʾēl ʾel-gôyim hammôrəḏîm* 'to the sons of Israel, to nations that are rebelling'. The plural *gôyim*, used of Israel, is unusual. The LXX has no 'nations' and reads 'to the house of Israel, those who embitter me', and many commentators delete *gôyim* as a gloss (Zimmerli, *Ezekiel 1*, Hermeneia). The MT is translated, as in the ASV (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). *bənê yiśrāʾēl* is 'sons of Israel', as at 37:16, 21.

*ʿaḏ-ʿeṣem hayyôm hazzeh* 'to this very day' is literally 'to the bone of this day', an idiom of exact identity (Gen 7:13; 17:23).

paragraphs.text: וְהַבָּנִ֗ים קְשֵׁ֤י פָנִים֙ וְחִזְקֵי־לֵ֔ב אֲנִ֛י שׁוֹלֵ֥חַ אוֹתְךָ֖ אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה׃

i18n.en: And the sons are hard of face and strong of heart; I am sending you to them, and you shall say to them, 'Thus says the Lord YHWH.'

notes.official:
*qəšê p̄ānîm wəḥizqê-lēḇ* 'hard of face and strong of heart' is rendered literally; the ASV paraphrases it as 'impudent children and stiffhearted'. The 'hard/strong' vocabulary (*ḥzq*) runs through 2:4-3:9 and plays on the prophet's name *yəḥezqēʾl*, 'El strengthens' (see 3:8-9).

*kōh ʾāmar ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* 'Thus says the Lord YHWH' (`adonai-yhwh`): the message the prophet is to deliver is set in single quotes inside the divine speech.

paragraphs.text: וְהֵ֙מָּה֙ אִם־יִשְׁמְע֣וּ וְאִם־יֶחְדָּ֔לוּ כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵ֑מָּה וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י נָבִ֖יא הָיָ֥ה בְתוֹכָֽם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And they — whether they hear or whether they refrain, for they are a rebellious house — they shall know that a prophet has been among them.

notes.official: *ʾim-yišməʿû wəʾim-yeḥdālû* 'whether they hear or whether they refrain': *ḥāḏal* is 'cease, hold back' (ASV 'forbear'). The pair recurs at 2:7 and 3:11, 27. *bêṯ məri* 'a rebellious house' is Ezekiel's name for Israel in the commission (2:5-8; 3:9, 26-27; 12:2-3). *nāḇîʾ* 'prophet' as everywhere in the corpus (`navi-first-occurrence-abraham`).

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָ֠דָם אַל־תִּירָ֨א מֵהֶ֜ם וּמִדִּבְרֵיהֶ֣ם אַל־תִּירָ֗א כִּ֣י סָרָבִ֤ים וְסַלּוֹנִים֙ אוֹתָ֔ךְ וְאֶל־עַקְרַבִּ֖ים אַתָּ֣ה יוֹשֵׁ֑ב מִדִּבְרֵיהֶ֤ם אַל־תִּירָא֙ וּמִפְּנֵיהֶ֣ם אַל־תֵּחָ֔ת כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃

i18n.en: And you, son of human, do not be afraid of them, and do not be afraid of their words, though briers and thorns are with you and you sit among scorpions; do not be afraid of their words, and do not be dismayed at their faces, for they are a rebellious house.

notes.official: *kî sārāḇîm wəsallônîm ʾôṯāḵ* 'though briers and thorns are with you'. Both nouns are rare: *sallôn* recurs only at 28:24 ('brier'), and *sārāḇ* occurs only here. The ASV 'briers and thorns' is kept. A derivation of *sārāḇîm* from Aramaic *srb* 'be refractory' ('though rebels ... are with you') is possible but uncertain (HALOT s.v.), and the botanical pair suits the parallel 'you sit among scorpions'.

paragraphs.text: וְדִבַּרְתָּ֤ אֶת־דְּבָרַי֙ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אִֽם־יִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְאִם־יֶחְדָּ֑לוּ כִּ֥י מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: You shall speak my words to them, whether they hear or whether they refrain, for they are rebellious.

notes.official: *kî məri hēmmâ* 'for they are rebellious' is literally 'for they are rebellion'; the abstract noun stands for the people. Some manuscripts and versions read 'a rebellious house' as in vv 5-6 and 8. The MT is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם שְׁמַע֙ אֵ֤ת אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִי֙ מְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ אַל־תְּהִי־מֶ֖רִי כְּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֑רִי פְּצֵ֣ה פִ֔יךָ וֶאֱכֹ֕ל אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֖י נֹתֵ֥ן אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: But you, son of human, hear what I am speaking to you: do not be rebellious like the rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat what I am giving you."

notes.official: *pəṣēh p̄îḵā* 'open your mouth' (*pāṣâ*, used also of the earth opening its mouth, Gen 4:11) prepares the eating of the scroll in 3:1-3. Unlike the 'rebellious house', the prophet is to take in what he is given. The speech that began in 2:3 closes here. For the canon's quotation of this verse see the reception note at 2:1.

paragraphs.text: וָאֶרְאֶ֕ה וְהִנֵּה־יָ֖ד שְׁלוּחָ֣ה אֵלָ֑י וְהִנֵּה־ב֖וֹ מְגִלַּת־סֵֽפֶר׃

i18n.en: I looked, and behold — a hand was stretched out to me, and behold, in it was a scroll of a book.

notes.official: *wəhinnēh-yāḏ šəlûḥâ ʾēlay* 'a hand was stretched out to me'. The hand is not identified, as at 8:3 ('the pattern of a hand'). *məḡillat-sēp̄er* 'a scroll of a book' (Jer 36:2, 4; Ps 40:8) modernizes the ASV 'a roll of a book' without changing the sense (`megillat-sefer-scroll-written-front-and-back-ezekiel-2-3`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּפְרֹ֤שׂ אוֹתָהּ֙ לְפָנַ֔י וְהִ֥יא כְתוּבָ֖ה פָּנִ֣ים וְאָח֑וֹר וְכָת֣וּב אֵלֶ֔יהָ קִנִ֥ים וָהֶ֖גֶה וָהִֽי׃ (ס)

i18n.en: He spread it out before me, and it was written on the front and on the back; and written on it were laments, and mourning, and woe.

notes.official:
*wəhîʾ ḵəṯûḇâ pānîm wəʾāḥôr* 'and it was written on the front and on the back'. *pānîm* and *ʾāḥôr* are 'face' and 'rear' (NRSV 'on the front and on the back'). The KJV/ASV idiom 'within and without' says the same thing, but a modern reader may take it as the inside and outside of a container (`megillat-sefer-scroll-written-front-and-back-ezekiel-2-3`). Scrolls were normally written on one side only, so commentators note the detail; Greenberg (*Ezekiel 1-20*, AB 22) takes it to mean the scroll was full. Rev 5:1 ('written within and on the back') echoes this verse.

*qinîm wāhegeh wāhî* 'laments, and mourning, and woe': *hegeh* is a low sound such as a moan or rumble (Job 37:2; Ps 90:9), and *hî* occurs only here, as a by-form of the cry *nəhî*.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes 2:9-10 ('the roll of a book ... written within and without'). It reads the two-sided writing as something remarkable for its time and the eating of the scroll (3:3) as Ezekiel taking in its knowledge. The line renders *pānîm wəʾāḥôr* literally.
